title: Attune Retail — Workshop: latency & cost decomposition for edge-forward deployments
summary: Workshop-run benchmarking for Attune Retail POC focused on latency decomposition, throughput ceilings, and 1M-token cost estimates across three candidate deployment topologies (hosted, dedicated, edge-private). Goal: actionable recommendations for a low-latency in-store recommender prototype.
content:
Context:
Attune Retail (customer) is building an in-store recommendation assistant that needs sub-200ms P95 response for short prompt flows (<= 120 tokens) and predictable monthly inference costs. This doc records the workshop bench runs we executed 2026-09-14 -> 2026-09-17, raw results, quick decompositions, and recommended next steps for the POC.

Goals and success criteria (customer-facing):
- P95 latency <= 200ms for single-turn prompts of ~80 tokens at steady-state.
- Support burst concurrency up to 80 RPS with graceful degradation.
- < $150 per 1M tokens for production traffic with dedicated setup; better for hosted if caching helps.

Test matrix (runs):
1) Hosted API baseline (redwood-hosted, eu-west)
   - Model: open-13B-qat (float16, Redwood-verified)
   - Hardware: multi-tenant H100 pool (shared)
   - Concurrency profiles: 1, 5, 20, 80 RPS
   - Batch config: automatic continuous batching (Redwood defaults)

2) Dedicated reserved (customer-dedicated queue)
   - Model: open-13B-qat (float16) and quant-13B-int8
   - Hardware: 2x A100-80GB dedicated nodes (pinned)
   - Autoscale: disabled for the run (steady capacity)
   - Concurrency: 1..120 RPS
   - Manual batching: bs=4,8,16 tested

3) Edge-private (on-prem gateway + small GPU)
   - Model: quant-13B-int8 and small-7B-qat (fallback)
   - Hardware: single V100-equivalent node (customer dev edge appliance, ~16GB GPU memory) behind 50ms local network
   - Concurrency: 1..40 RPS
   - Config: KV-cache disabled (warm runs), tokenizer on-host

Workload and dataset:
- 1,200 sample queries from anonymized Attune session logs (short intent queries, average prompt 62 tokens, average generated tokens 48). File: attune-retail-sample-1.2k.jsonl
- Synthetic burst script used for concurrency shaping and steady-state: bench/attune_burst_v2.py (GitHub PR linked above).

Key observations (high-level):
- Hosted baseline: P50 ~ 60ms, P95 ~ 210-240ms at 1-5 RPS; P95 climbs non-linearly beyond 20 RPS due to multi-tenant preemption; throughput unstable at >40 RPS. Cost estimate before caching: $190–$220 per 1M tokens.
- Dedicated A100: P50 ~ 38ms, P95 ~ 110ms at 1-20 RPS with bs=8 batching; hits ~95 RPS sustained with bs=8 and streaming enabled. Cost estimate: ~$110 per 1M tokens (amortized committed capacity).
- Edge-private (single small GPU): P50 ~ 110ms, P95 ~ 420ms for quant-13B-int8; switching to small-7B reduces P95 to ~160ms but has quality regressions on rare product-specific intents. Cost on appliance (CapEx amortized) estimated equivalent $85 per 1M tokens at current projected utilization but has limited headroom for bursts.

Measured results (representative numbers):
Hosted (open-13B-qat, eu-west, shared H100):
- 1 RPS: P50=55ms, P95=210ms, tokens/sec=320
- 5 RPS: P50=62ms, P95=230ms, tokens/sec=1.6k
- 20 RPS: P50=80ms, P95=380ms, tokens/sec=6.4k (tail volatility observed)
- 80 RPS: service errors 2.7%, P95 > 900ms
- Cost: measured (api-metering) ~ $0.00022 per token = ~$220 per 1M tokens

Dedicated (2x A100-80GB, open-13B-qat):
- bs=4, 5 RPS: P50=45ms, P95=170ms, sustained 18 RPS
- bs=8, 20 RPS: P50=38ms, P95=110ms, sustained 95 RPS (kv-cache warm)
- bs=16, 40 RPS: P50=60ms, P95=150ms, throughput plateau 110 RPS (diminishing returns)
- Cost: reserved commit: $8,400/mo (example); measured per-token cost ~ $0.00011 = ~$110 per 1M tokens (including infra + ops estimate)

Edge-private (quant-13B-int8 on 16GB GPU):
- 1 RPS: P50=95ms, P95=420ms
- 5 RPS: P50=120ms, P95=540ms, started queueing at 12 concurrent requests
- 20 RPS: queue depth increased, observed request failures if concurrency unmanaged
- small-7B-qat fallback: P95 ~160ms at 20 RPS, but end-user relevancy drops on 7% of intents in eval set
- Cost: appliance amortized estimate $0.000085 per token = ~$85 per 1M tokens (assumes 60% utilization and 36-month amortization)

Latency decomposition (representative hosted-run p95 = 230ms):
- Network RTT (eu-west, client->edge->hosted): 38ms
- Ingress parsing + auth: 12ms
- Queuing and batching delays: 44ms (higher at >20 RPS)
- Model forward and tokenization: 120ms
- Response serialization + egress: 16ms
- Notes: when KV-cache hits are present, model forward reduces by ~30–40ms on average for typical Attune prompts.

Throughput ceiling analysis:
- Dedicated A100 with bs=8 hits efficient GPU utilization around 90 RPS for the 13B model; further increases require multi-node sharding or larger batch sizes which increase latency.
- Hosted pool variability is the limiting factor for tight SLOs. Observed preemption/GC patterns cause latency spikes at moderate concurrency.
- Edge appliance cannot sustain high burst concurrency without a small request queue or secondary routing to dedicated nodes.

Cost sensitivity and knobs tested:
- Quantization: moving from float16 to int8 reduced per-token runtime by ~22% and lowered memory pressure; cost improvement notable on dedicated and edge runs but introduced 1–3% quality lift on some nuanced product-description prompts.
- Batching: bs=8 produced best latency/throughput tradeoff for Attune's short responses. Larger batches improved throughput slightly but increased P95 latency.
- KV-cache: prefix caching for repeat session patterns reduced model work ~18% across the sample set and decreased cost per 1M tokens by ~15% in hosted runs when cache hit rates were ~30%.

Qualitative quality note:
- Quant-13B-int8 had occasional tokenization artifacts on long product SKUs and rare brand names; customer requires >98% fidelity on product name correctness. Small-7B fallback preserved correctness only ~92% of the time on those edge cases. Recommendation: keep 13B quant in the loop for final token generation for product identifiers; use small model for short contextual suggestions when latency critical.

Recommendations (actionable):
1) For Attune Retail POC launch target (in-store assistant, constrained latency): use Dedicated A100 reserved capacity with bs=8, KV-cache enabled, and quant-13B-int8 where acceptable. This meets P95 < 200ms in our tests at realistic RPS and keeps cost near customer target.
2) Edge strategy: deploy small-7B-qat locally for initial latency-sensitive suggestions with a routed fallback to Dedicated for final ranking/generation where correctness matters. Implement client-side prefetch + local caching to keep local calls sub-150ms.
3) Hosted as short-term ramp: start on Redwood Hosted with explicit burst routing and a dedicated capacity reservation for peak windows; use caching and response streaming to reduce tail. Avoid relying on multi-tenant only for low-latency SLOs.
4) Next engineering steps: enable token-level tracing for 1 week, capture a representative KV-cache hit matrix, and run longer 72-hour soak tests on dedicated infra to validate tail behavior. Create a canary route that fails over to hosted/dedicated depending on queue length.

Workshop notes / open questions (items for customer follow-up):
- Customer needs clarity on acceptable quality degradation for quantized weights on product identifiers (confirm threshold).
- SLA vs cost tradeoff: would Attune accept a hybrid model where 30% of traffic resolves locally and 70% uses dedicated cloud? This impacts reserved commit sizing.
- Hardware guidance: customer is evaluating an in-store appliance spec; recommend minimum 24GB GPU for future headroom (M40/V100-class not recommended).

Appendix A — exact benchmark commands (high level):
- bench script used: python bench/attune_burst_v2.py --model open-13B-qat --workers 8 --batch 8 --duration 300 --concurrency 20 --dataset attune-retail-sample-1.2k.jsonl --trace-output traces/hosted-20rps.json
- Dedicated run orchestration used redwoodctl: redwoodctl deploy --model open-13B-qat --nodes 2 --gpu a100-80 --batching manual --batch-size 8; monitor with redwoodctl tail --route attune-retail-dedicated

Appendix B — raw CSV summary (selected rows):
- hosted,1rps, P50=55ms, P95=210ms, tokens_sec=320, cost_per_m=220
- dedicated,20rps, bs=8, P50=38ms, P95=110ms, tokens_sec=8000, cost_per_m=110
- edge,5rps, quant13,int8, P50=120ms, P95=540ms, tokens_sec=700, cost_per_m=85

Appendix C — suggested tickets / next tasks:
- Create ENG ticket to add per-token fidelity checks on product identifiers during quant onboarding (ENG-1294).
- Solutions: implement fallback routing prototype (PR linked).
- Customer workshop scheduled 2026-09-22 to review recommended commit sizing and edge appliance spec.

Notes to self (workshop artifacts):
- Save bench traces to s3://redwood-bench/attune/2026-09-14/ (already uploaded).
- Follow up with Attune infra contact (Liam O.) for appliance power/thermal constraints.

Concluding remark:
Dedicated reserved capacity with modest batching and KV-cache enabled is the pragmatic path to meet Attune Retail's latency and cost targets for the POC. Edge appliances can be part of a hybrid topology but need careful routing, local caching, and a plan for final quality-critical generation to be executed in the cloud.

Document author: Priya Nambiar — Solutions Engineering
